source: Written 2026-10-16 from the verified oracle text (Scryfall via carddb --verify, fetched 2026-10-16) for every card a scene shows or names, Scryfall's rulings (Witherbloom, the Balancer; Sprout Swarm; Up the Beanstalk; Chatterfang, Squirrel General; Zulaport Cutthroat; Exsanguinate; Bloodchief Ascension; Archfiend of Despair; Grievous Wound; Mirkwood Bats, The Master of Lake-town and Pox Plague have none published) and this deck's notes. Cards a caption names are [[bracketed]] so clips.py checks them against the current list; [[Exsanguinate]] is the sorcery card, never Stensian Sanguinist's prepare spell. Opponents' cards are placeholders, never named. The only power and toughness stated are the tokens' (Sprout Swarm's 1/1 Saproling, Chatterfang's 1/1 Squirrels, Army of the Damned's 2/2 Zombies). Commander starting life is 40 (CR 903.7). The discount: affinity is CR 702.41a; Witherbloom grants it to your instants and sorceries only while it is on the battlefield (CR 113.6), its own affinity applies as it is cast, and the first cast pays no tax (CR 903.8). Affinity counts every creature you control, tapped ones included. A generic reduction cuts only the generic part of a cost (CR 118.7a), never below {0} (CR 601.2f), and never changes mana value (CR 202.3; Witherbloom ruling), so Up the Beanstalk still sees 8 and 9. Woodland Cemetery enters untapped beside a Swamp or a Forest (oracle text); dorks cast on turns 1 and 2 tap from the next turn on (CR 302.6). The loop: buyback is an additional cost (CR 702.27a, 601.2b), added before reductions come off (CR 601.2f), so {1}{G} plus {3} with four creatures, Witherbloom included, costs {G}; convoke pays a colored pip by tapping an untapped creature of that color (CR 702.51a), even one that just arrived (Sprout Swarm ruling); buyback puts the card into your hand instead of your graveyard as it resolves (CR 702.27a, 608.2n). An instant can be cast whenever you have priority (CR 117.1a). A repeatable loop is proposed as a shortcut with a number of repetitions (CR 732.2a), and each opponent may shorten it to respond (CR 732.2b). Saprolings made in an opponent's end step untap in your untap step (CR 502.3) and can attack, having been yours since your turn began (CR 302.6). One event with several occurrences triggers once for each (CR 603.2c): a Saproling and a Squirrel made together trigger Mirkwood Bats twice, one Zulaport drain triggers The Master once for each opponent who lost life, and every milled card triggers Bloodchief Ascension. Chatterfang's Squirrels are a replacement effect (CR 614.1a). Dies means put into a graveyard from the battlefield (CR 700.4); sacrifice is CR 701.21a. X is generic mana (CR 107.4b), announced before the total cost is figured (CR 107.3a, 601.2b, 601.2f), so 50 creatures pay all of X=50; a sorcery waits for your main phase with the stack empty (CR 307.1); players can lose more life than they have (Exsanguinate ruling). The Master: damage causes loss of life (CR 120.3a); mill is CR 701.17a, and a short library mills what it has (CR 701.17b); a player at 0 or less life loses, and so does one who tried to draw from an empty library (CR 704.5a, 704.5b), checked whenever a player would get priority (CR 704.3). Bloodchief Ascension's abilities have intervening 'if' clauses (CR 603.4); one opponent must have lost 2 or more, and it adds at most one counter a turn (rulings). Archfiend counts only life lost, and the amount is figured as its trigger resolves (rulings). Pox Plague rounds each half down (oracle text; CR 107.1a), so with Archfiend out an even life total is gone at the end step, and an odd one is left at 1 unless that player lost other life that turn. Grievous Wound's enchant player makes it target a player as it is cast (CR 702.5a, 303.4a), and its trigger resolves after the damage (ruling: 10 life, 1 damage, 9, then lose 5).

scenes.head: Witherbloom, the Balancer — black-green combo
scenes.sub: Each creature you control makes your instants and sorceries {1} cheaper. Go wide, then cast big spells for their pips.
scenes.say: Witherbloom, the Balancer. Black-green combo, where each creature you control makes your instants and sorceries one cheaper. Go wide, then cast the big spells for their colored mana.

scenes.head: Affinity on every instant and sorcery
scenes.sub: Instant and sorcery spells you cast cost {1} less per creature you control, tapped or not. Only generic mana comes off; the pips stay.
scenes.say: Witherbloom gives every instant and sorcery you cast affinity for creatures: one less for each creature you control, tapped or untapped. Only generic mana comes off. The colored pips always stay.

scenes.head: Turn 2: four creatures
scenes.sub: [[Llanowar Elves]] came down on turn 1. Its {G}, a Forest and a Swamp cast [[Elvish Mystic]], [[Birds of Paradise]] and [[Viscera Seer]], one mana each.
scenes.say: Turn two: four creatures. Llanowar Elves came down on turn one. Now its green mana, a Forest and a Swamp cast Elvish Mystic, Birds of Paradise and Viscera Seer, for one mana each.

scenes.head: Turn 3: Witherbloom for four
scenes.sub: It has affinity for creatures too: {6}{B}{G}, minus four creatures, is {2}{B}{G}. Mystic and Birds then cast [[Up the Beanstalk]], which draws a card.
scenes.say: Turn three: Witherbloom for four mana. It has affinity for creatures itself, so four creatures take four off its eight. Then Mystic and Birds cast Up the Beanstalk, which draws a card as it enters.

scenes.head: Turn 4: [[Army of the Damned]] for {B}{B}{B}
scenes.sub: Five creatures take off all five generic. It's still mana value 8, so [[Up the Beanstalk]] draws a card. Thirteen tapped 2/2 Zombies arrive.
scenes.say: Turn four: Army of the Damned for three black. Five creatures take off all five generic. A discount doesn't change mana value, so it's still an eight, and Up the Beanstalk draws a card. Thirteen tapped Zombies arrive.

scenes.head: Turn 5: [[In Garruk's Wake]] for {B}{B}
scenes.sub: Eighteen creatures, but only its seven generic come off. It destroys every creature and planeswalker you don't control. Mana value 9: another card.
scenes.say: Turn five: In Garruk's Wake for two black. You have eighteen creatures, but only its seven generic can come off. It destroys every creature and planeswalker you don't control, and Up the Beanstalk draws again.

scenes.head: Then [[Rise of the Dark Realms]], {B}{B} too
scenes.sub: Every creature card in every graveyard comes onto the battlefield under your control, including every one [[In Garruk's Wake|the Wake]] sent there.
scenes.say: Then Rise of the Dark Realms, also two black. Every creature card in every graveyard comes onto the battlefield under your control, including every one the Wake just sent there. The Beanstalk draws again.

scenes.head: Count your creatures before every spell
scenes.sub: Next: the loop, its kills, and three combos that don't need Witherbloom.
scenes.say: Count your creatures before every instant and sorcery. Next: the infinite loop, how it kills, and three combos that don't need Witherbloom.

scenes.head: [[Sprout Swarm]]: the loop
scenes.sub: {1}{G} instant, convoke, buyback {3}: create a 1/1 green Saproling. Pay buyback, and the card returns to your hand as it resolves.
scenes.say: Sprout Swarm: the loop. An instant for one and a green, with convoke and buyback three. It makes a one-one green Saproling, and if you paid buyback, it returns to your hand.

scenes.head: With buyback: {4}{G}, minus four
scenes.sub: Buyback adds {3}, and it's generic. Witherbloom and three more creatures make four, so affinity takes off all four generic: the cast costs {G}.
scenes.say: With buyback it costs four and a green, minus four. Buyback adds three, and it's generic. Witherbloom and three more creatures make four, so affinity takes off all four generic, and the cast costs one green.

scenes.head: Their end step: cast it
scenes.sub: An instant can wait: cast it with buyback in the end step of the last opponent before you. A [[Forest]] pays the {G}.
scenes.say: Wait for the end step of the last opponent before your turn. Sprout Swarm is an instant, so cast it then, with buyback, and tap a Forest for the green.

scenes.head: A Saproling, and the card comes back
scenes.sub: It resolves: a 1/1 green Saproling enters untapped, and buyback puts Sprout Swarm into your hand instead of your graveyard.
scenes.say: It resolves. A one-one green Saproling enters untapped, and buyback puts Sprout Swarm back into your hand instead of your graveyard.

scenes.head: Cast it again: convoke with the Saproling
scenes.sub: Five creatures, still {G}. Convoke lets you tap a green creature instead of paying {G}, even one that just arrived: tap the Saproling.
scenes.say: Cast it again, and convoke with the Saproling. Five creatures now, and it still costs one green. Convoke lets you tap a green creature instead of paying it, even one that just arrived. Tap the Saproling.

scenes.head: Each cast taps one Saproling and makes one
scenes.sub: Saproling 2 pays for cast three, Saproling 3 for cast four. No limit, so name a number: fifty casts, fifty Saprolings.
scenes.say: Each cast taps one Saproling and makes another: Saproling two pays for the third cast, three for the fourth. So name a number: fifty casts, fifty Saprolings. Opponents can still respond to any of them.

scenes.head: Why their end step
scenes.sub: Your turn is next: every Saproling untaps and can attack, since you've controlled it since your turn began. No opponent gets a main phase first.
scenes.say: Why their end step? Your turn is next, so every Saproling untaps and can attack: you've controlled it since your turn began. And no opponent gets a main phase to answer them first.

scenes.head: Witherbloom, three more creatures, Sprout Swarm
scenes.sub: That's the whole loop. Next: three ways to win with the Saprolings.
scenes.say: Witherbloom, three more creatures and Sprout Swarm: that's the whole loop. Next, three ways to win with the Saprolings.

scenes.head: Three ways to cash in the Saprolings
scenes.sub: [[Mirkwood Bats]] drains as they arrive. [[Zulaport Cutthroat]] drains as they die. [[Exsanguinate]] turns the whole board into its X.
scenes.say: Three ways to cash in the Saprolings. Mirkwood Bats drains as they arrive. Zulaport Cutthroat drains as they die. And Exsanguinate turns your whole board into its X.

scenes.head: [[Mirkwood Bats]]: every token drains
scenes.sub: Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses 1 life. No outlet needed: each Saproling the loop makes costs every opponent 1.
scenes.say: Mirkwood Bats: every token drains. Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses one life. No sacrifice outlet needed: each Saproling the loop makes costs every opponent one.

scenes.head: With the Bats out, the loop is the kill
scenes.sub: Each cast makes one Saproling, so each opponent loses 1. Forty casts take 40 life from every opponent.
scenes.say: With the Bats out, the loop itself is the kill. Each cast makes one Saproling, so each opponent loses one life. Forty casts take forty life from every opponent at the table.

scenes.head: [[Chatterfang, Squirrel General|Chatterfang]]: two tokens a cast
scenes.sub: If tokens would be created under your control, that many 1/1 green Squirrels are created too. A Saproling and a Squirrel: the Bats trigger twice.
scenes.say: Chatterfang makes it two tokens a cast. If tokens would be created under your control, that many green Squirrels come too. A Saproling and a Squirrel: the Bats trigger twice, and twenty casts do it.

scenes.head: Or sacrifice them: [[Zulaport Cutthroat]]
scenes.sub: Whenever it or another creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1. [[Viscera Seer]] sacrifices one for no mana, tapped or not: fifty Saprolings, fifty life.
scenes.say: Or sacrifice them. Whenever Zulaport Cutthroat or another creature you control dies, each opponent loses one, and you gain one. Viscera Seer sacrifices a creature for no mana, even a tapped one: fifty Saprolings, fifty life.

scenes.head: More drains, more free outlets
scenes.sub: [[Blood Artist]]: whenever any creature dies, target player loses 1. [[Carrion Feeder]], [[Woe Strider]], [[Yahenni, Undying Partisan|Yahenni]] and [[Umbral Collar Zealot]] sacrifice for free.
scenes.say: More drains, more free outlets. Blood Artist makes a target player lose one whenever any creature dies. Carrion Feeder, Woe Strider, Yahenni and Umbral Collar Zealot sacrifice creatures for no mana.

scenes.head: Your main phase: [[Exsanguinate]] for {B}{B}
scenes.sub: A sorcery: loop on their end step, cast it on your turn. X is generic, so with 50 creatures X=50 costs {B}{B}. Each opponent loses 50.
scenes.say: On your turn, Exsanguinate. It's a sorcery, so loop on their end step first. X is generic mana: with fifty creatures, an X of fifty costs just two black. Each opponent loses fifty, and you gain it all.

scenes.head: Pick the finisher you drew
scenes.sub: The Bats need nothing else. Zulaport needs a free outlet. Exsanguinate needs your main phase.
scenes.say: Pick the finisher you drew. The Bats need nothing else. Zulaport needs a free outlet. And Exsanguinate needs your main phase.

scenes.head: Two cards, no [[Witherbloom, the Balancer|Witherbloom]] needed
scenes.sub: [[The Master of Lake-town]] makes life loss mill. Once [[Bloodchief Ascension]] is charged, each card an opponent mills costs them 2 life.
scenes.say: The Master of Lake-town and Bloodchief Ascension: two cards, no Witherbloom needed. Life loss makes them mill, and once the Ascension is charged, each milled card costs two life.

scenes.head: [[The Master of Lake-town]]: life loss mills
scenes.sub: Whenever a player loses life, that player mills that many cards. Damage counts, and so does your own life loss.
scenes.say: The Master of Lake-town: whenever a player loses life, that player mills that many cards. Damage counts, since damage causes loss of life. And it's any player, so you mill too.

scenes.head: [[Bloodchief Ascension]]: charge it first
scenes.sub: At the beginning of each end step, if an opponent lost 2 or more life this turn, you may put a quest counter on it.
scenes.say: Bloodchief Ascension needs three counters first. At the beginning of each end step, if an opponent lost two or more life this turn, you may put a quest counter on it: every player's end step.

scenes.head: Charge it with your drains
scenes.sub: With [[Zulaport Cutthroat]] out, sacrifice two creatures to [[Viscera Seer]]: each opponent loses 2, and that end step adds a counter. Do it on three turns.
scenes.say: Charge it with your drains. With Zulaport Cutthroat out, sacrifice two creatures to Viscera Seer: each opponent loses two, and that end step adds a counter. The Seer works on any turn: three turns, three counters.

scenes.head: Three counters: each card costs 2
scenes.sub: Whenever a card is put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, you may have that player lose 2 life, and you gain 2.
scenes.say: With three counters, every card costs them two. Whenever a card is put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, you may have that player lose two life. If you do, you gain two.

scenes.head: One point of life loss feeds itself
scenes.sub: They lose 1: [[The Master of Lake-town|The Master]] mills 1. That card costs 2 life, which mills 2. Those cost 4, which mills 4, and so on.
scenes.say: Then one point of life loss feeds itself. They lose one, so The Master mills one. That card costs them two life, which mills two. Those two cost four, which mills four, and so on.

scenes.head: It ends when their life or library does
scenes.sub: Each milled card costs 2 life: 20 cards take 40. A shorter library empties first; they lose when they next draw.
scenes.say: It ends when their life or library runs out. Every milled card costs two life, so twenty cards take forty. A shorter library empties first, and they lose when they next draw.

scenes.head: One drain starts every opponent's loop
scenes.sub: [[Zulaport Cutthroat]] makes each opponent lose 1. The Master triggers for each: all three mill, and all three loops run.
scenes.say: One drain starts every opponent's loop. Zulaport Cutthroat makes each opponent lose one, and The Master triggers for each of them: all three mill, and all three loops run.

scenes.head: [[Archfiend of Despair]]: every loss, twice
scenes.sub: At the beginning of each end step, each opponent loses life equal to the life that player lost this turn.
scenes.say: Archfiend of Despair: every loss, twice. At the beginning of each end step, each opponent loses life equal to the life that player lost this turn. And your opponents can't gain life.

scenes.head: Turn 7: [[Pox Plague]] for five Swamps
scenes.sub: {B}{B}{B}{B}{B} has no generic, so [[Witherbloom, the Balancer|Witherbloom]] takes nothing off. Archfiend came down last turn at full price too: it's a creature.
scenes.say: Turn seven: Pox Plague, for five Swamps. It's five black pips and no generic, so Witherbloom takes nothing off. The Archfiend came down last turn at full price too: it's a creature.

scenes.head: Everyone loses half, rounded down: you too
scenes.sub: Opponents at 40, 30 and 24 drop to 20, 15 and 12. Then everyone discards half their hand and sacrifices half their permanents: keep the Archfiend.
scenes.say: Everyone loses half, rounded down, and that includes you. Opponents at forty, thirty and twenty-four drop to twenty, fifteen and twelve. Then each player discards half their hand and sacrifices half their permanents. Keep the Archfiend.

scenes.head: Your end step: the same half again
scenes.sub: Each opponent loses the life they lost this turn: 20, 15 and 12 more. All three hit 0.
scenes.say: At your end step, the same half again. Archfiend makes each opponent lose the life they lost this turn: twenty, fifteen and twelve more. All three hit zero.

scenes.head: Odd life totals end at 1
scenes.sub: At 31, [[Pox Plague|Pox]] takes 15, then the end step 15: 1 left. One more point that turn is lethal, like a creature sacrificed with [[Zulaport Cutthroat]] out.
scenes.say: An odd life total leaves them at one. At thirty-one, Pox takes fifteen and the end step fifteen more. Lose one more point that turn and it's lethal: sacrifice a creature to Pox with Zulaport Cutthroat out.

scenes.head: [[Grievous Wound]] enchants a player
scenes.sub: Cast it on an opponent. Enchanted player can't gain life. Whenever they're dealt damage, they lose half their life, rounded up.
scenes.say: Grievous Wound enchants a player, so cast it on an opponent. The enchanted player can't gain life, and whenever they're dealt damage, they lose half their life, rounded up.

scenes.head: One point of damage, then half, then twice
scenes.sub: A 1/1 Saproling connects: 39. The Wound takes half, rounded up: 19 left. At your end step, Archfiend takes the 21 they lost: dead.
scenes.say: One point of damage, then half, then twice. A one-one Saproling connects: forty becomes thirty-nine, and the Wound takes half, rounded up, leaving nineteen. At your end step, Archfiend takes the twenty-one they lost.

scenes.head: Witherbloom, the Balancer
scenes.sub: Bracket 4 · four two-card combos · the full plan is in the Plan tab.
scenes.say: Witherbloom, the Balancer. Bracket four, with four two-card combos. The full plan is in the Plan tab.
